title: Count the digits
hints: Run the starter. It prints the right count for 345, but the test sees `None`. What does a function give back when it never says `return`?
Now try 0. The starter's loop never runs, so it counts 0 digits. But 0 is written with one digit.
Start `count` at 1 and keep dividing while `n >= 10`.

answer.explain: The starter prints instead of returning, so the caller gets `None`. It also says 0 has no digits. The reference starts at `count = 1` and divides by 10 while `n >= 10`: 345, 34, 3 gives a count of 3, and 0 never enters the loop and stays at 1.
